# Vendor/

Self-contained MuPDF build from upstream source, keeping `swift build` independent
of Homebrew or other system installs.

## Contents

- `build-mupdf.sh` — downloads the official MuPDF source tarball
  (`https://mupdf.com/downloads/archive/mupdf-<version>-source.tar.gz`), verifies its
  pinned SHA-256 checksum, and compiles `MuPDF.xcframework`.
- `MUPDF_VERSION` — the upstream tag currently targeted (1.24.8).
- `MuPDF.xcframework` — generated by `build-mupdf.sh` and excluded from Git. A single
  combined static library (MuPDF core + bundled thirdparty codecs), arm64 (Apple Silicon)
  only, built with PDF JavaScript (mujs) and OCR (tesseract/leptonica) disabled.
  Consumed by `Package.swift` as a local `.binaryTarget`.

The corresponding public C headers are vendored separately at
`Sources/MuPDFBridge/include/mupdf/` (needed for `#include <mupdf/fitz.h>`
in `MuPDFBridge.h`) — `build-mupdf.sh` updates both together.

## Bumping the MuPDF version

1. Pick the new release tag from https://mupdf.com/releases/history.
2. `./Vendor/build-mupdf.sh <new-version>` — it downloads the tarball, verifies
   it against the pinned sha256 in the script (update `MUPDF_SHA256` there
   first, or export `MUPDF_SHA256=...` for a one-off run, using the value the
   script prints on a mismatch after you've verified the download), builds,
   and overwrites `Vendor/MuPDF.xcframework` and
   `Sources/MuPDFBridge/include/mupdf/`.
3. Update `Vendor/MUPDF_VERSION` and the default in `build-mupdf.sh`.
4. `swift build && swift test`, skim upstream `CHANGES` for anything that
   touches APIs this app calls (`Sources/MuPDFBridge/MuPDFBridge.c`), then
   commit.

The script's own output flags two known Clang-Modules pitfalls from vendoring
someone else's header tree wholesale under an `umbrella header` (which sweeps
in every physical file under the directory, whether or not it's actually
`#include`d):
- A new header-guardless X-macro-style snippet header (like
  `mupdf/pdf/name-table.h`) needs a `textual header "mupdf/..."` entry in
  `include/module.modulemap`, or Clang corrupts its mid-declaration textual
  inclusion with cryptic "expected identifier" parse errors.
- A new header unreachable from `fitz.h`/`pdf.h` (like `mupdf/html.h`) needs
  an `exclude header "mupdf/..."` entry, or every build prints a "does not
  include header" warning for it.
Both are just noise/warnings the script surfaces proactively so a version
bump doesn't have to rediscover them the hard way; add the printed line(s) to
`include/module.modulemap` and re-run.

## Why not link against Homebrew's mupdf?

Homebrew's formula builds against system freetype/harfbuzz/openjpeg/etc and
enables JS + OCR by default, which means: (a) an extra install step for every
contributor/CI machine, (b) hardcoded `/opt/homebrew` paths that break on
Intel Macs or non-Homebrew setups, and (c) a build that can silently change
underneath the app on `brew upgrade`. Building from MuPDF's own source
tarball with its bundled thirdparty libraries avoids all three and pins an
exact, reproducible version.

## Why not a prebuilt MuPDF XCFramework from someone else?

There isn't one to reuse — checked as of this writing there's no official or
actively-maintained community MuPDF XCFramework/Swift package (Swift Package
Index and GitHub searches both come up empty). If that changes upstream, it
would be worth revisiting.
